question: Give me an overview of how this application is structured.
key_facts: It is a Spring Boot web application using Spring MVC controllers that render Thymeleaf templates.
Code is organised by feature into packages such as owner, vet, system and model.
Persistence uses Spring Data JPA repositories (e.g. OwnerRepository, VetRepository, PetTypeRepository).
It uses an H2 database by default, with MySQL and PostgreSQL available as alternatives.

question: Which database does the app use by default, and how do you switch it to MySQL or PostgreSQL?
key_facts: The default database is H2 (database=h2 in application.properties).
Schema and data scripts are chosen per database via db/${database}/schema.sql and data.sql.
MySQL or PostgreSQL is selected with a Spring profile (application-mysql.properties / application-postgres.properties) that sets the database and datasource URL.

question: Where is the owner search by last name implemented?
key_facts: OwnerController.processFindForm handles GET /owners.
It calls OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith (prefix match on last name) with paging.
When exactly one owner matches it redirects to that owner's details page.
When nothing matches it rejects the lastName field with a 'notFound' error and shows the find form again.

question: Where are pet form inputs validated, and what rules are enforced?
key_facts: PetValidator.validate checks that the name is present and at most 30 characters.
PetValidator requires a type for new pets and requires a birth date.
PetValidator is registered for the 'pet' model attribute via @InitBinder in PetController.
PetController additionally rejects birth dates in the future and duplicate pet names for the owner.

question: Where and how is the list of vets cached?
key_facts: VetRepository's findAll methods are annotated @Cacheable("vets").
CacheConfiguration enables caching (@EnableCaching) and creates the 'vets' cache through a JCacheManagerCustomizer.
The cache is configured with statistics enabled.

question: How is the UI language chosen, and how can a user switch it?
key_facts: WebConfiguration defines a SessionLocaleResolver with English as the default locale.
A LocaleChangeInterceptor switches the language from the 'lang' request parameter (e.g. ?lang=de).
Translations come from messages/messages*.properties files.

question: Which code converts the pet type chosen in the form into a PetType object?
key_facts: PetTypeFormatter (a Spring Formatter<PetType>) does the conversion.
Its parse method loads all types with PetTypeRepository.findPetTypes and returns the one whose name matches the text.
If no type matches it throws a ParseException ('type not found').

question: Walk me through what happens when a user books a new visit for a pet.
key_facts: The form posts to /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/new, handled by VisitController.processNewVisitForm.
Before the handler runs, the @ModelAttribute method loadPetWithVisit loads the owner and pet (failing if either is missing) and attaches a new Visit to the pet.
A visit date that is not after today is rejected.
On success it calls owner.addVisit(petId, visit), saves the owner, and redirects to the owner page with a 'Your visit has been booked' message.

question: How does the app prevent an owner from having two pets with the same name?
key_facts: When adding a pet, processCreationForm checks owner.getPet(name, true) and rejects the name as 'duplicate'.
The name comparison is case-insensitive (equalsIgnoreCase in Owner.getPet).
The database also has a unique constraint unique_owner_pet_name on (owner_id, name).
A DataIntegrityViolationException from that constraint is caught and turned into the same duplicate-name error.

question: When an owner's details are updated, how does the code guard against editing the wrong owner?
key_facts: processUpdateOwnerForm compares the owner id from the form with the ownerId path variable.
On a mismatch it rejects the 'id' field and redirects back to the edit form with an error message.
The @InitBinder in OwnerController disallows binding the id fields ('id', '*.id') from request parameters.

question: What is the difference between the /vets and /vets.html endpoints?
key_facts: /vets.html renders the vets/vetList HTML page, paginated 5 vets per page.
/vets returns a Vets object as the response body (@ResponseBody) for JSON/XML clients, containing all vets.
Both read vets through VetRepository.

question: What happens when a request hits /oups?
key_facts: CrashController handles GET /oups and deliberately throws a RuntimeException.
It exists to showcase error handling; the error is rendered by the error.html template.

question: Which endpoints create and edit pets, and where does their URL prefix come from?
key_facts: GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/new create a pet.
GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/edit edit a pet.
The /owners/{ownerId} prefix comes from the class-level @RequestMapping on PetController.

question: Which Spring Boot version and Java version does the project target?
key_facts: The Maven parent is spring-boot-starter-parent version 4.1.0.
The Java version is 17.

question: Which libraries provide caching in this project?
key_facts: spring-boot-starter-cache provides Spring's caching support.
javax.cache:cache-api provides the JCache (JSR-107) API.
Caffeine is the runtime cache provider.

question: Where is the number of owners shown per page in search results defined?
key_facts: It is pageSize = 5 in OwnerController.findPaginatedForOwnersLastName.

question: How does the application authenticate users and restrict access to admin pages?
key_facts: States that the application has no authentication or authorization: there is no login and no Spring Security dependency or configuration.

question: Which endpoint deletes an owner, and what happens to their pets?
key_facts: States that there is no endpoint for deleting owners (owners can only be created, searched, viewed and edited).

question: Give me an overview of the backend architecture.
key_facts: backend/app/main.py creates the FastAPI app and includes api_router under settings.API_V1_STR (/api/v1).
Routes are split into login, users, utils, items and private modules, and the private routes are only included in development.
Data models are SQLModel classes in models.py stored in PostgreSQL, with Alembic migrations.
Configuration comes from a pydantic-settings Settings class in core/config.py.

question: How does the frontend call the backend API, and where is the auth token attached to requests?
key_facts: The frontend uses a generated API client in frontend/src/client.
frontend/src/main.tsx configures the client's baseURL from VITE_API_URL and its auth from the access_token stored in localStorage.
On 401 or 403 responses the token is removed and the user is redirected to /login.

question: Where is a user's password checked when they log in?
key_facts: POST /login/access-token (login_access_token in api/routes/login.py) handles login.
It calls crud.authenticate, which looks the user up by email and calls verify_password.
A wrong email or password returns 400 'Incorrect email or password'; an inactive user gets 400 'Inactive user'.

question: Where is the JWT access token created, and how long is it valid?
key_facts: core/security.py create_access_token encodes 'exp' and 'sub' claims with SECRET_KEY using HS256.
Validity is ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES, which defaults to 60 * 24 * 8 minutes (8 days).
login_access_token creates the token for the authenticated user's id.

question: Where and when is the first superuser account created?
key_facts: init_db in core/db.py creates a superuser from FIRST_SUPERUSER and FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD if no user with that email exists.
init_db is called from app/initial_data.py.
scripts/prestart.sh runs 'alembic upgrade head' and then initial_data.py.

question: Which dependency restricts endpoints to superusers, and which endpoints use it?
key_facts: get_current_active_superuser in api/deps.py raises 403 ('The user doesn't have enough privileges') if the current user is not a superuser.
It protects the user-administration endpoints: listing users, creating users, and updating or deleting a user by id.
It also protects POST /utils/test-email/ and POST /password-recovery-html-content/{email}.

question: Explain the password reset flow end to end.
key_facts: POST /password-recovery/{email} creates a reset token and emails it only if the user exists, but always returns the same message (to avoid revealing which emails are registered).
The reset token is a JWT whose subject is the email and which expires after EMAIL_RESET_TOKEN_EXPIRE_HOURS (48 hours by default).
POST /reset-password/ verifies the token with verify_password_reset_token, loads the user, and updates the password via crud.update_user.
An invalid token and an unknown user both return 400 'Invalid token'; an inactive user is rejected.

question: How does login avoid revealing through response time whether an email is registered?
key_facts: When no user has that email, crud.authenticate still calls verify_password against a fixed DUMMY_HASH, so the response takes about as long as a real check.

question: How are password hashes upgraded when the hashing scheme changes?
key_facts: core/security.py configures pwdlib PasswordHash with Argon2 (preferred) and Bcrypt.
verify_password uses verify_and_update, which returns a new hash when the stored one uses an outdated scheme.
crud.authenticate saves the updated hash on the user when one is returned.

question: When listing items, which items does each kind of user see?
key_facts: GET /items/ (read_items) returns all items for superusers.
Other users only get items whose owner_id is their own id.
Results are ordered by created_at descending, paginated with skip/limit, and include a total count.

question: What happens to a user's items when the user is deleted?
key_facts: Their items are deleted too: User.items is a Relationship with cascade_delete=True.
Item.owner_id is a foreign key to user.id with ondelete='CASCADE'.
Superusers are not allowed to delete themselves (403).

question: How does the backend stop a deployment from running with default secrets?
key_facts: A Settings model validator checks SECRET_KEY, the database password and FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD for the value 'changethis'.
Outside development it raises a ValueError; with FASTAPI_ENV=development it only issues a warning.

key_facts: POST /login/access-token and POST /users/signup are public.
POST /password-recovery/{email} and POST /reset-password/ are public.

question: Is there an endpoint that creates users without authentication, and when is it enabled?
key_facts: Yes: POST /private/users/ in api/routes/private.py creates a user with no authentication dependency.
The private router is only included when FASTAPI_ENV is 'development'.

question: Which PostgreSQL driver does the backend use, and how is the database URL adapted for it?
key_facts: The driver is psycopg (version 3, psycopg[binary]).
A Settings field validator rewrites postgres:// or postgresql:// URLs to postgresql+psycopg://.

question: Where is the backend health check defined, and what uses it?
key_facts: GET /api/v1/utils/health-check/ in api/routes/utils.py returns True.
The backend service's Docker Compose healthcheck curls that URL.

question: Where is rate limiting on the login endpoint implemented?
key_facts: States that the codebase does not implement rate limiting for login (no limiter middleware, dependency or proxy rule).

question: How does the backend use Redis for caching?
key_facts: States that the backend does not use Redis or any caching layer (no Redis dependency or service).
